analysis.title: GS Abbas - GS US Daily Download 5 Nov 2026
key_insights: Brent fell about $18 over five days, one of its biggest 5-day declines in recent history. Energy underperformed Consumer Discretionary by about 15 points over the last 5 sessions.

Since 1952, the 12 months after a midterm election have been the S&P 500's strongest stretch of the four-year cycle. Across 18 midterms the index averaged +7.5% through year end, +13.9% over 6 months and +15.5% over 12 months, and was higher at both the 6-month and 12-month points in all 18 cases.

GS Macro says Democrats won the House and Senate with larger-than-expected majorities. GS expects them to use fiscal deadlines to seek limits on the war with Iran, a rollback of selected tariffs and a reversal of last year's spending cuts.

Federal AI and data center regulation is unlikely to change because it would still need bipartisan Senate support and a veto override. Democratic wins at the state and local level are likely to bring short-term data center moratoria, potentially affecting about 45% of planned US data center capacity expansion.

Utilities after the midterms: GS sees the Texas governor outcome as a possible negative for exposed stocks, the Georgia PSC outcome as a possible negative for SO, and the Ohio governor outcome as less constructive for FE and AEP. A possible California special legislative session before November 15 could help PCG, SRE and EIX.

Qualcomm: GS expects the stock to trade modestly lower after an in-line quarter and better revenue guidance. Datacenter momentum is offsetting smartphone weakness from memory-related demand destruction. GS keeps its Neutral rating.

ARM: GS expects the stock to be range bound after revenue and EPS guidance above the Street. Licensing revenue was stronger than expected and royalty revenue was significantly lower and again missed expectations. GS stays Sell rated.

AppLovin Q3'26: core gaming grew nearly 50% YoY, and consumer business spend was up triple digits % YoY with positive trends into Q4. Management cited high operating leverage and FCF generation supporting buybacks.

Market update: Trump told the NYT he would accept the election results, which removed some left tail risk. Crude fell 8% and Brent went back to about $95, through the $100 level, which renewed an index-level bid across markets.

Retail rose 5.5%, about 390 bps ahead of SPY, the 2nd largest 1-day outperformance in the last 2 years. XRT is at 5-year highs and XLP is at all-time highs. Consumer was the largest beneficiary of lower yields and oil, light positioning and views of less spending pressure from budget and debt negotiations.

The GS floor activity level was 6 out of 10, finishing +2% better to buy. Asset manager and hedge fund net flows were about balanced. The largest theme was net buying of hyperscalers against supply in semis. GS says the election backdrop favors owners of compute (hyperscalers) and hurts those who build out, sell into or power datacenters (neoclouds, semis, power).
Exchange volumes were 30%+ above the 20-day average. Post-bell moves: QCOM -4%, ZG -22% on revenue and EBITDA misses, APP +15% on a big beat and guidance well above expectations.

sector_views.rationale: Democratic state-level wins could raise near-term uncertainty around data center development, particularly in Texas and Georgia. GS still sees these as important long-term load growth markets.
Retail rose 5.5% on lower yields and oil, light positioning and less expected spending pressure. This is a description of flows and performance, not a formal GS rating.
GS says the new political backdrop is bad for those who must build out, sell into or power datacenters. This is a flow observation, not a formal rating.

earnings_insights: QCOM FQ4 (reported 11/4 after close): in-line quarter, better revenue guidance, 'solid' revenue guide with EPS and EBIT mixed. Stock -4% post bell. Datacenter momentum offset by smartphone headwinds.

ARM (reported after close 11/4): headline revenue and EPS guidance above the Street. Licensing revenue was stronger than expected with four new CSS customers, and royalty revenue was significantly lower and missed expectations. Management has increased confidence in up to $2bn of AGI CPU revenue in FY27-28.
APP Q3'26 (reported after close 11/4): big beat and guidance well above expectations. Core gaming up nearly 50% YoY and consumer business spend up triple digits % YoY. Stock +15% post bell.
ZG (reported after close 11/4): misses on revenue and EBITDA, stock -22% post bell.
